transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good afternoon Mr. Okonkwo. I wanted to come by and talk to you about how the laparoscopic surgery went.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you doctor. I am just glad to be awake. I hope everything went as planned.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Actually, there was a complication during the procedure. A surgical clip was placed on the wrong anatomical structure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: The wrong structure? What does that mean?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, during the laparoscopic approach, the visualization can be tricky, and a clip was applied to a vessel that didn't need one. It required us to perform an additional maneuver to correct the placement and ensure there was no vascular compromise.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't quite follow. Are you saying someone made a mistake inside me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry. It was our mistake, and I apologize for the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very distressing. I am a man of standing in my community. If word gets out that there were mistakes in my surgery, people will wonder if I am fit to lead or if my health is more fragile than it is. My family expects me to return home strong.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. But the important thing is that the clip was identified while you were still under anesthesia.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You aren't listening to me. My reputation is built on strength. To have an error like this, it makes me feel vulnerable in a way that is hard to explain to my sons.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really have to get to the ward for rounds soon, but we caught the error.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are rushing me? I am trying to tell you how this affects my life outside this hospital.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it is upsetting, but the surgical team corrected the clip and your vitals are stable now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Stable vitals do not fix the worry in my heart. Was this something that could have killed me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Not necessarily, because we corrected it immediately. It just meant the surgery took a bit longer than we initially planned.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I am being managed, not heard. Why did this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The anatomy in the pelvic region can be quite variable, and the clip just went on the wrong spot.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So it was the anatomy? Or it was the doctor?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: As I said, I apologize for the error. We take full responsibility for it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: If you take responsibility, then what happens now? How do we make sure this doesn't happen again or that there aren't other mistakes I don't know about?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep monitoring your recovery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. I want to know exactly what the follow-up is. When will I see the lead surgeon?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll have to check the schedule. We'll probably see you at the next check-up.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is too vague. I need a date. I need to know what to tell my family about why the surgery took longer.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can't give you a specific date right this second, but we'll keep you posted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are dismissing me. I am sitting here telling you I am distressed and you are telling me to stay tuned.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not dismissing you, but let's wrap this up so I can check on my other patients. The main point is that you are safe.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I am safe, perhaps, but I do not feel respected.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry you feel that way.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are sorry I feel that way, but you are not listening to what I am saying.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Look, we've covered the facts. The clip was misplaced, we fixed it, and you are recovering.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: And my concerns about my family and my community?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can discuss that later if you like. For now, just focus on resting.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I cannot rest when I feel the person treating me is in such a hurry to leave the room.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really do have to go now. I'll send someone in with your medications.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is very disappointing.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll be in touch.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('have to get to the ward', 'wrap this up', 'really do have to go now') and shows defensive escalation.

E.justification: The error was named explicitly, but the resident never performed a comprehension check.

A.justification: Resident used direct apology language ('I am sorry', 'I apologize') and explicitly stated 'We take full responsibility' while maintaining this under pushback.

R.justification: Patient's emotional bids regarding his reputation and vulnerability were consistently met with factual redirection and dismissals.

T.justification: The resident provided only placeholders ('keep monitoring', 'probably see you at the next check-up', 'keep you posted') with no specific dates or roles.
